nodes.description: Proxy implementation slot at keccak256("PROXIABLE") = 0xc5f16f0fcc639fa48a6947836d9850f504798523bf8c9a3a87d5876cf622bcf7, holding the address of the delegatecall target logic contract.

constructor(bytes memory constructData, address contractLogic) public - writes the logic address into the proxy slot and performs a delegatecall to it for initialization, then emits myEvent and requires success.
fallback() external payable - loads the stored logic address, copies raw calldata and delegates execution to the implementation, forwarding return data or reverting.
Calldata bytes forwarded verbatim to the delegatecall during construction (initialization payload).
Caller-supplied address of the logic/implementation contract; stored in the proxy slot and used as the delegatecall target.
delegatecall(constructData) executed inside the constructor against an arbitrary, caller-controlled logic address, running untrusted code in the storage context of the proxy.
delegatecall(gas(), contractLogic, ...) inside fallback using raw calldata and the address read from the proxy storage slot, executing the implementation in the proxy's storage context.
Inline assembly sstore to the fixed keccak256("PROXIABLE") slot, persisting the implementation address without any visibility of Solidity storage layout.
bool success returned by the constructor's delegatecall, used in require(success, "Construction failed").
bytes memory __ holding the raw return data of the constructor delegatecall, later emitted via myEvent(__).
Assembly local variable set from sload of the proxy slot in fallback(), used as the delegatecall destination.

edges.reason: constructor unconditionally delegates execution to a caller-supplied address, allowing arbitrary code to run in the proxy storage context with no validation or access restriction.
delegatecall transfers execution to externally supplied code during construction, which can re-enter the proxy or manipulate its storage before initialization completes.
constructor execution reaches the inline assembly sstore that persists contractLogic into the fixed proxy slot.
the contractLogic parameter (fully attacker-controlled at deployment) flows directly into the delegatecall target, enabling arbitrary code execution.
contractLogic is written verbatim into the keccak256("PROXIABLE") storage slot, so the caller controls the implementation address used by every future fallback call.
the constructData byte payload is passed unchanged as calldata to the delegatecall, becoming the selector and arguments executed by the logic contract.
the boolean success result of the delegatecall is captured in the local variable used by require.
the returndata of the delegatecall is captured in the local bytes variable that is emitted in myEvent.
fallback forwards all unknown calldata to the stored implementation address via delegatecall with no selector or caller filtering.
delegatecall in fallback hands full execution and storage control to external code, which may call back into the proxy or alter the implementation slot.
the logic address read from the keccak256("PROXIABLE") slot determines the delegatecall target, so whoever can write that slot controls all fallback execution.
the assembly sload of the proxy slot populates the local contractLogic variable inside fallback.
the locally loaded implementation address is used directly as the delegatecall destination for arbitrary callers.

normalization_plan.reason: constructData is a non-core parameter whose only purpose is to supply the calldata consumed by the constructor's delegatecall, so it is absorbed into that unsafe operation node.
contractLogic is a non-core parameter whose first and most security-relevant use is being persisted into the fixed proxy storage slot by the sstore unsafe operation.
successFlag is a non-core local holding the delegatecall success flag guarded by require; it is ephemeral and belongs to the constructor function node.
the __ bytes local only carries the delegatecall returndata emitted by myEvent and has no independent semantic role outside the constructor.
logicAddrFallback is a non-core assembly local that immediately becomes the delegatecall target in fallback, so it merges into that unsafe operation.
